description_en: The monument is situated on a terrace along the left bank of the Pādukā River (Pādukā Khola) and is one of the northernmost structures within the pilgrimage site of Pādukāsthān. To the north of it lies the Pādukāsthān Jvālā Mandira (DLK0270).Pādukāsthān is a significant area within the larger region known as Pañcakośī, attracting pilgrims from various parts of western Nepal. These sites are renowned for their flame temples, where natural gas flames are believed to mark the locations where different parts of Satī's body fell while Śiva carried her charred remains (Lecomte-Tilouine 2009). Pādukāsthān specifically marks the spot where Satī's feet (pādukā) landed.The monument itself comprises a small square room with two protruding walls. Constructed using cut stone blocks and mud masonry, the structure also incorporates reused carved blocks originating from medieval temples. There are indications that the place may have previously functioned as a shrine dedicated to Gaṇeśa, as evidenced by the presence of a high-relief stone statue of the deity situated above the lintel (DLK0271-001). Although the statue was photographed in 2014, it was absent from its niche during the 2022 assessment, and its current whereabouts are unknown. The lintel itself features a low-relief image of Gaṇeśa. Above the lintel and the vacant niche, an exquisitely carved rosette is placed, likely originating from a medievalśikharatemple.
references: REFERENCES Lecomte-Tilouine, Marie. 2009, “The Panchakoshi of Dullu. The Fire Frame of the Malla Imperial Capital”, in Bards and Mediums. History, Culture and Politics in the Central Himalayan Kingdoms , Marie Lecomte-Tilouine (ed.). Almora: Almora Book Depot, pp. 253-276.
